transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Terrace CTO), Elena (Terrace Security), Sam (Terrace Infra), Dina (Product)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro: I'm Alex Kim, AE for Redwood, and Priya Nair is our SE. We're here to understand Terrace's private deployment requirements and see whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private (VPC) is the right fit. Marcus, do you want to kick off with what you've been evaluating?

[00:25] Marcus (Terrace CTO): Yeah, sure. Thanks Alex. We're building several customer-facing features that use LLMs for financial summarization and automated underwriting. Data is sensitive — PII and transaction metadata — so compliance and network isolation are must-haves. We've looked at Redwood hosted but legal pushed back; they want either Dedicated in our VPC or a private deployment that never leaves our network.

[00:50] Alex: Got it. Totally normal. Priya, I think you can drive the technical constraints.

[00:55] Priya (Redwood SE): Yep. Marcus, quick questions as a starting point: which cloud and regions are you using today? Any multi-account org setup?

[01:08] Sam (Infra): We're on AWS. Prod lives in us-east-1 and us-west-2. We run core infra in a centralized security account and tenant workloads in separate accounts — typical landing zone. We'll likely need private endpoints in both regions. Also we use Transit Gateway to connect VPCs; peering can be contentious because of scale.

[01:30] Priya: Good — that helps. So primary asks we usually see: 1) ability to keep traffic inside the customer's VPC (no public internet egress), 2) PrivateLink/private endpoint access from app subnets, 3) support for cross-account access and peering/Transit-GW patterns, and 4) KMS integration for key control. Does that map to you?

[01:50] Elena (Security): Yes. Additionally: audit logs must be delivered to our SIEM, retention for 3 years, SOC2 compliant controls, and we need SSO via SAML/Okta for RBAC. Also, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS — we prefer HSM-backed CMKs.

[02:10] Alex: Great. On all those, Redwood Private supports VPC deployment with private endpoints and optional no-internet egress configurations. For KMS we integrate with customer-managed keys; HSM-backed CMKs are supported through standard KMS workflows. We also produce audit logs that can be forwarded to your S3 or CloudWatch — from there to your SIEM. We'll share our security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts after the call.

[02:40] Marcus: A couple specifics: latency SLO is important for our underwriting flows — target p95 token latency under 300ms for small prompts. Can Redwood guarantee that inside our VPC? If we run in us-east-1, we'd prefer model variants pinned to the same AZs.

[03:00] Priya: Latency is a balance of model size, instance type, and network hops. For p95 under 300ms we typically recommend a Dedicated pool pinned to specific AZs with GPU types we can size for concurrency. Private deployments on customer VPCs minimize network hops. We can run benchmarking against your sample prompt set to validate.

[03:25] Sam: For network, we have strict egress rules — only approved endpoints via PrivateLink. Does Redwood support AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) as an option rather than VPC peering?

[03:40] Alex: Yes, we support both models. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is often preferred for security teams because it avoids peering and limits exposure. For high throughput real-time workloads, peering or Transit Gateway sometimes gives lower overhead, but it's dependent on your TGW setup. We can lay out tradeoffs.

[04:00] Priya: To add, with PrivateLink we can expose a regional private endpoint per region. If you need cross-region calls, either route across your TGW or replicate Redwood Private nodes in each region. There is some replication cost but it keeps latency low.

[04:20] Elena: Replication cost is ok if it's necessary. More important: do you support private DNS so our service names resolve to the interface endpoint? We can't have developers needing to manually set endpoint IPs.

[04:35] Priya: Yes, we can provide a private DNS option for the endpoints so the standard API host resolves to the interface endpoint inside your VPC. We'll also provide manifests to automate Route53 private zone entries.

[04:50] Marcus: Good. Also we use strict CIDR ranges. We need to avoid overlapping ranges with any Redwood-managed subnets. How do you handle those allocations?

[05:02] Alex: For Private deployments, we typically ask customers to allocate subnets for Redwood workers in their VPC. We provide a recommended naming and sizing guide: one or more private subnets per AZ, with security group and IAM role configs. There's no need to hand over our CIDRs; we operate inside your ranges. We'll include the exact CIDR sizing in the checklist.

[05:25] Sam: What about egress to model download repositories during initial model provisioning — if there's no internet egress, how do we get the model artifacts?

[05:36] Priya: Two options: 1) we can stage model artifacts into your S3 bucket (you provide a bucket/policy) and the deployment pulls from there, or 2) allow a one-time restricted egress window from the deployment to our artifact endpoint which we can log and audit. Many customers prefer the S3 staging pattern for full control.

[05:55] Elena: The S3 staging sounds better. We'll need the exact role/policy templates so security can pre-approve.

[06:05] Alex: We'll include those as IaC snippets in the checklist — CloudFormation/Terraform examples.

[06:12] Dina (Product): A question on network per-app segmentation: we want multiple Redwood endpoints for different products with separate usage accounting and RBAC. Is that supported in private deployments?

[06:24] Priya: Yes — Redwood supports per-route model configs and API keys. In Private mode we can run multiple routes with separate API keys mapped to RBAC groups via your SAML provider. We'll describe best practices for isolating workloads either via multiple clusters or logical routing inside a single deployment depending on scale.

[06:46] Marcus: About updates and rollouts — we can't have unpredictable updates causing regressions. How do canaries and rollbacks work in Private?

[06:55] Priya: We support canary rollouts and pinned model versions; the control plane can be run in your account or a Redwood-managed control plane with private connectivity depending on your preference. Rollouts can be staged by percentage and we have automatic fallback policies. We can also do manual approvals for production rollouts.

[07:15] Elena: If the control plane is managed by Redwood, how do we get auditability and SSO integration?

[07:23] Alex: For managed control planes, we expose audit logs and integrate with your SAML/Okta. If you'd rather self-host the control plane in your account, we provide an option where you manage auth and we only operate the runtime. That increases isolation but also your operational burden.

[07:40] Sam: One more infra detail — do you support VPC endpoints across accounts (cross-account interface endpoints)? Our app accounts need to call the Redwood service in the central infra account.

[07:52] Priya: Yes, interface endpoints can be configured cross-account. We provide the endpoint service name and your infra can create an endpoint in the calling account that references the service in the host account. We'll add documented steps.

[08:05] Marcus: Great. On compliance: SOC2 is a baseline. Can you share encryption-at-rest specifics and whether we can bring our own CMK for data keys?

[08:17] Alex: You can bring your own CMK. Data at rest uses envelope encryption; we integrate with your KMS for the data key encryption. We also support HSM-backed CMKs if your KMS is HSM backed. We'll attach architecture diagrams in the checklist.

[08:32] Elena: What about logs retention and separation? We need logs to be pushed into our S3 with deterministic partitioning and we want the ability to revoke access quickly.

[08:42] Priya: We can configure log delivery to your S3 buckets with configurable prefixes and lifecycle rules. For quick revocation, you can rotate KMS keys or update bucket policies. We'll describe typical playbooks.

[08:58] Sam: For benchmarking — we want to simulate our workload: 500 concurrent users, median prompt length 80 tokens, some requests with streaming. Can Redwood run benchmarks inside our VPC?

[09:10] Priya: Yes — we'll coordinate a benchmark where we deploy a temporary load generator inside your VPC or use your load testing harness to hit the private endpoint. We'll need sample prompt set, expected concurrency profile, and preferred times. Priya to own scheduling.

[09:25] Marcus: Perfect. Pricing: we prefer committed Dedicated vs pay-as-you-go for predictability. Any rough guidance today?

[09:33] Alex: High level: Dedicated/reserved capacity gives better per-token economics and more predictable latency; Private deployments have similar pricing but include deployment/operational add-ons (control plane option, support tiers). I'll send a rough TCO comparison and an initial pricing band in the follow-up.

[09:50] Elena: Are there any known limitations on model types — e.g., we use some quantized variants and custom fine-tuned weights. Can those be loaded?

[10:00] Priya: We support a broad model catalog and can load customer-provided fine-tuned models if they are compatible with our runtime. Quantized models generally work if they match one of our supported quant formats. For custom weights we'll need to validate the format and may do a small onboarding test.

[10:18] Alex: Quick logistics: we'll send three artifacts after this call: 1) Private deployment checklist + IaC snippets, 2) security whitepaper + SOC2 evidence summary (link), and 3) a benchmark plan template. Links will be in the follow-up email.

[10:33] Marcus: That sounds good. Any blockers from your side?

[10:37] Alex: None. From Redwood's side, we just need the VPC CIDRs, list of accounts, and a sample prompt set for sizing.

[10:47] Dina: One last question — do you provide guidance for cost controls, e.g., token quotas per route, alerting?

[10:55] Priya: Yes — Redwood Console supports token-level cost breakdowns, per-route quotas, and alerting. We'll include examples of policies customers use to cap spend.

[11:10] Marcus: Ok let's recap.

[11:13] Alex: Recap: Redwood will send checklist, security docs, and pricing; Priya will schedule a benchmark with Sam; Marcus will share VPC CIDRs and regions; and we'll include IaC for endpoints, S3 staging, and KMS roles. Action items are in the notes.

[11:33] Elena: Thanks. Please make sure the checklist includes PrivateLink vs TGW pros/cons and the model artifact staging steps.

[11:40] Alex: Will do. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by email and schedule the benchmark.

[11:47] (call ends)

Shared artifacts mentioned in call:
- Private deployment checklist (to be attached)
- Security whitepaper & SOC2 summary (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/whitepaper.pdf)
- IaC examples (Terraform module link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-sample)
- Benchmark plan template (sheet link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark-plan)

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker overlap and some audio artifacts in the first 2 minutes. Some product names transcribed imperfectly (e.g., K V cache typed as "K V cache").
